request.system:
You are checking an operations research model before it is solved. Read the word problem and list what any correct formulation of it must contain. Don't write the model, and don't solve the problem.

The model's decision variables are listed by name in <variables>. Use exactly those names and no others. If a requirement needs a quantity that isn't one of them, put it in cannot_express instead.

- variables: for each listed name, say whether it counts whole things ("integer": vehicles, trips, people, products, servings), measures a divisible quantity ("continuous": kilograms, acres, hours, money), or the text supports both ("unclear"). Quote the words that decide it.
- objective: its direction (min or max) and its terms over the listed names, with the numbers exactly as given. Quote the words it comes from.
- requirements: every requirement the text states, as a linear inequality or equation over the listed names. Use the numbers exactly as given, and write percentages as fractions (30% as 0.3). Quote the exact words each one comes from.
  - strict: true if the wording is strict ("more than", "must exceed", "fewer than"); still write it with >= or <=.
  - could_be_equal: true if the wording names no inequality at all ("twice as many as", "three times the number of"), so "=" would be a fair reading too.
  - scope: "combined" if one limit covers several items together, "per item" if it applies to each item separately, "single" if it involves one quantity. Decide this from the text: "at most 50 cakes of either type" may be one total or one limit per type, so quote why.
  - Leave out non-negativity, unless the text says a quantity can be negative.
- not_requirements: every sentence that states a preference, a motivation, popularity, or background rather than a requirement ("prefers", "is more popular", "would like", "sells better"), with its quote, why it isn't a requirement, and the inequality someone might wrongly make of it (empty terms if there's none). Never turn one of these into a requirement.
- cannot_express: each requirement that needs a quantity not among the listed names, with its quote and the quantity it needs.
- Don't add anything the text doesn't state.

<problem>
Welcome to the challenge of optimizing the logistics network of a futuristic city, connected by an advanced transportation system comprising 8 crucial nodes. This city's system is designed to maximize the efficiency of goods transport from the central distribution hub to a primary delivery station, passing through various checkpoints and distribution centers along the way.

Here's a detailed view of the transportation capacities (in thousands of units) that each route can handle:

- From Node 0 (Source): Can dispatch goods to Node 1 (3 units), Node 2 (7 units), Node 3 (2 units), Node 4 (18 units), Node 5 (18 units), Node 6 (14 units), and Node 7 (10 units).
- From Node 1: Can send goods to Node 0 (1 unit), Node 2 (10 units), Node 3 (16 units), Node 4 (14 units), Node 6 (6 units), and Node 7 (10 units).
- From Node 2: Can transport goods to Node 0 (4 units), Node 3 (7 units), Node 4 (2 units), Node 5 (2 units), Node 6 (6 units), and Node 7 (10 units).
- From Node 3: Can move goods to Node 0 (2 units), Node 1 (3 units), Node 2 (7 units), Node 4 (20 units), Node 5 (8 units), Node 6 (6 units), and Node 7 (10 units).
- From Node 4: Can dispatch goods to Node 0 (1 unit), Node 1 (20 units), Node 2 (4 units), Node 3 (8 units), Node 5 (13 units), Node 6 (8 units), and Node 7 (1 unit).
- From Node 5: Can send goods to Node 0 (16 units), Node 1 (9 units), Node 2 (17 units), Node 3 (17 units), Node 4 (11 units), Node 6 (7 units), and Node 7 (8 units).
- From Node 6: Can transport goods to Node 0 (3 units), Node 1 (7 units), Node 2 (14 units), Node 3 (1 unit), Node 4 (20 units), Node 5 (5 units), and Node 7 (13 units).
- From Node 7 (Destination): Can receive goods from Node 0 (3 units), Node 1 (6 units), Node 2 (5 units), Node 3 (1 unit), Node 4 (14 units), Node 5 (20 units), and Node 6 (9 units).

A capacity of "0" indicates there is no direct route available between those two nodes.

The goal is to determine the maximum amount of goods (in thousands of units) that can be transported from the central distribution hub (Node 0) to the primary delivery station (Node 7) without exceeding the transport capacity of any route.

What is the optimal value of goods (in thousands of units) that can be transported from the source to the destination?
</problem>
